scope: Theorem 5.1 of the manuscript “Lipschitz Equivalent Separable Banach Spaces Need Not Be Linearly Isomorphic” (preprints/Lipschitz-Equivalent-Separable-Banach-Spaces-Need-Not-Be-Linearly-Isomorphic-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 324 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cc670229303a1ed9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are finite-dimensional Euclidean coordinate spaces Un, U = ( L n≥1 Un)2, and a bijection h : U ⊕2 ℓ2 → U fixing zero, such that 24 25 ∥x − x′ ∥ ≤ ∥h(x) − h(x′ )∥ ≤ 26 25 ∥x − x′ ∥. (5.1) Moreover, D = h − πU has local orthogonality: for every finite family of distinct points x1, . . . , xm there are neighborhoods Oj of xj, an integer l, and mutually orthogonal coordinate subspaces Hj ⊂ ( L n≥l Un)2 such that P≥lD(Oj) ⊂ Hj (1 ≤ j ≤ m). Here P≥l is the projection onto blocks with index at least l, and a coordinate subspace is the closed span of a subset of the specified orthonormal coordinates.
